messages:
Mike: quick signal from canary: after merging kernel-selector v3 we see a tiny but persistent set of NaNs coming from long-ROPE runs (seq > 65k). Repro with internal-lm-small at seq=102400, dim=2048. stack points at rotary_packed_fp16 path producing sin/cos NaNs.

Aria: yikes. any immediate mitigation ideas?

Mike: root cause is numeric headroom collapse for theta = base_freq * pos in the packed fp16 accumulation kernel. packed-fp16 wins selector scoring for latency so it got chosen. For very large pos theta overflows/underflows fp16 domain or loses precision and trig libs produce NaN.

Sam: can you paste the log and the minimal repro?

Mike: log: ``runtime: kernel=rotary_packed_fp16 pos=98765 dim=2048 theta=1.23e5 -> sin/cos produced NaN\ntensor_check: contains inf`` Repro script iterates pos up to 110k, batch=1.

Jenny: low-risk hotfix: make kernel selector consider a numeric headroom guard and prefer fp32-accum kernel when theta magnitude exceeds a threshold. Ship to canary ASAP.

Aria: proposed guard: if (!isfinite(theta) || fabsf(theta) > 1e4f) choose rotary_fp32_accum. Add instrumentation so we can see how often this fires.

Sam: quick prototype:
```
float theta = base_freq * (float)pos;
if (!isfinite(theta) || fabsf(theta) > 1e4f) {
  choose_kernel("rotary_fp32_accum");
}
```
I'll add a reproducer and unit tests covering positions [1e3,1e4,1e5,1e6].

Mike: two follow-ups: (1) perf impact for the rare huge-pos workloads (we should capture telemetry to quantify), (2) ALiBi uses exponent-like math so needs a similar safeguard.

Jenny: telemetry + alerts plan: emit metrics posenc.phase_wrap_count and kernel_selector.fallback_numeric_headroom. Add a non-paging alert and dashboard panels. Put unit tests in eng-runtime/kernels/test_posenc_numeric.py.

devops-bot: created ticket INF-2987 and scheduled canary window 2026-03-22 03:00 UTC.

Aria: for ALiBi I'd clamp slope/signal to avoid extreme exponents. Example clamp:
```
float slope = base_slope * bucket_idx;
if (!isfinite(slope) || fabsf(slope) > 1e3f) slope = copysignf(1e3f, slope);
```
Emit telemetry when clamp occurs.

Sam: ran microbenchmarks. If fallback triggers, worst-case latency regression ~6% on those synthetic huge-pos runs. Acceptable for correctness.

Jenny: longer-term proposals:
- add numeric_headroom() to encoder kernel API so selector can score kernels by numeric safety (bits of mantissa / exponent headroom) in addition to latency.
- consider compensated summation (Kahan) in fp16 accumulation as a configurable middle ground.
- add runtime config posenc.numeric_safety_mode = {auto|perf|safe}, default auto.

Aria: Kahan might help but needs measurement behind a flag. Also add docs blurb to runtime/positional-encoding.md describing the new flag and kernel selection behavior.

Mike: I'll open a short RFC: "Numeric headroom metric for kernel selection" — it will include API sketches, selector scoring formula (latency vs headroom), and a plan for gradual rollout. Also add RFC appendix with test vectors and perf matrices.

Jenny: immediate action items (hotfix):
- Mike: implement selector guard + telemetry + unit tests -> PR to canary
- Sam: attach reproducer + perf baseline to the PR
- Jenny: dashboard + lightweight alert (no page) for posenc.phase_wrap_count
- devops-bot: coordinate canary deploy after CI

Sam: PR incoming. Reproducer exercised locally and CI unit tests added.

Mike: rolling patch to canary now. If posenc.phase_wrap_count > 0 for >0.1% of requests we will evaluate rollback vs throttling.

Aria: also track kernel_selector.fallback_numeric_headroom rate and correlate with customer config (dedicated/private) so we know exposure.

Jenny: for ALiBi we should also cap slope scaling factor at model load time for user-provided slopes to prevent crafted inputs from triggering extremes.

Mike: RFC and follow-ups filed. Prioritize correctness and observability for this sprint; we'll iterate on performance safety tradeoffs after canary telemetry. :thumbsup:
